en: holiday travelers heading to their hometowns

examples.en: Ahead of the Lunar New Year, people heading to their hometowns are flooding in.

examples.ko: 귀성객을 위해 임시 열차를 더 운행해요.
examples.en: They run extra trains for people going home for the holiday.
The terminal was crowded all day with holiday travelers going home.

examples.ko: 올해 귀성객은 작년보다 줄어들 것 같아요.
examples.en: This year's hometown-bound travelers will probably be fewer than last year.

examples.ko: 고속도로 휴게소에서 귀성객에게 차를 나눠 줬어요.
examples.en: They handed out tea to holiday travelers at the highway rest stop.
Most people heading to their hometowns leave early in the morning.

explain: 설이나 추석 같은 명절에 고향으로 가는 사람들을 말해요. 고향에서 돌아오는 사람은 '귀경객'이라고 해요. '귀성길', '귀성 전쟁'처럼 명절 뉴스에서 자주 나와요.
explain_en: It refers to people going to their hometowns for holidays such as Seollal or Chuseok. People returning from their hometowns are '귀경객'. It appears often in holiday news in phrases like '귀성길' and '귀성 전쟁'.

examples.en: Difficulties get overcome as time passes.
My fear is being overcome little by little.

examples.ko: 가난은 노력만으로 극복되지 않을 때도 있어요.
examples.en: Sometimes poverty isn't overcome by effort alone.
I judged that the problem had been overcome.
I believe it's a problem that can be overcome.
The crisis was overcome with everyone's help.

explain: '이겨 내다'는 말로 많이 쓰고, '극복하다'는 내가 노력해서 이기는 것이에요. '극복되다'는 노력한 사람보다 문제가 해결된 결과에 초점을 둬서 글이나 뉴스에서 나와요.
explain_en: In speech '이겨 내다' is common; '극복하다' is overcoming something through your own effort. '극복되다' focuses on the problem having been resolved rather than who did it, and shows up in writing and news.

examples.ko: 아이가 길에 있는 웅덩이를 껑충 뛰어넘었어요.
examples.en: The child leaped over the puddle in the road.
The puppy sprang over the fence and ran away.
Vegetable prices have jumped a lot lately.

examples.ko: 우리 아들이 한 해 만에 키가 껑충 컸어요.
examples.en: My son shot up in height in just one year.
My score jumped up a lot on this exam.
The deer bounded into the forest.

explain: '깡충'보다 크고 다리가 긴 것이 뛰는 느낌이에요. 물가·점수·키가 갑자기 많이 오를 때도 '껑충 뛰다, 껑충 오르다'라고 말해요.
explain_en: It feels bigger than '깡충', like a long-legged animal leaping. It is also used when prices, scores or height rise suddenly, as in '껑충 뛰다' or '껑충 오르다'.

examples.ko: 전쟁을 피해 온 사람들이 난민촌에서 지내요.
examples.en: People who fled the war are staying in a refugee camp.
The news reported on winter life in the refugee camp.
They say water and medicine are lacking in the refugee camp.
A volunteer group sent blankets to the refugee camp.

examples.ko: 난민촌 아이들을 위한 학교가 문을 열었어요.
examples.en: A school for children in the refugee camp has opened.

examples.ko: 난민촌의 모습을 사진으로 본 적이 있어요.
examples.en: I have seen the refugee camp in photos.

explain: 뉴스나 기부 광고에서 주로 나오는 말이에요. 같은 뜻으로 '난민 캠프'라고도 하지만 기사에서는 '난민촌'이 더 자연스러워요.
explain_en: This word mostly appears in the news and donation ads. People also say '난민 캠프', but articles tend to use 난민촌.

examples.ko: 동북 지방은 겨울에 눈이 많이 와요.
examples.en: The northeast region gets a lot of snow in winter.
I want to travel to the northeast of China.
Korea is in Northeast Asia.
The typhoon is moving up toward the northeast.
A northeast wind is blowing, so it is chilly.
My neighborhood has a mountain to the northeast.

explain: '북동'도 같은 방향이에요. '동북아시아', '동북 지방'처럼 굳은 말은 '동북'을 써요. 중국 이야기에서 '동북 지방'은 보통 북동쪽에 있는 지역을 가리켜요.
explain_en: '북동' is the same direction, but set terms like '동북아시아' and '동북 지방' use '동북'. In talk about China, '동북 지방' refers to the region in the northeast.

examples.en: This song is a remake of an old song.
With a remake movie, you end up comparing it to the original.
I heard the news about the remake of that drama.
The remake became more popular than the original song.
I like the original better than the remake.
These days there are many remakes of foreign works.

explain: '리메이크'는 영화·드라마·노래를 다시 만든 작품이에요. 같은 줄거리를 새로 찍으면 '리메이크', 같은 노래를 다른 가수가 부르면 '리메이크 곡'이라고 해요. 원래 작품은 '원작', 원래 노래는 '원곡'이라고 불러요.
explain_en: 리메이크 is a movie, drama, or song made again. A newly filmed version of the same story is a 리메이크, and a song sung again by another singer is a 리메이크 곡. The original is called 원작, and the original song is 원곡.

examples.en: I feel a great sense of satisfaction after finishing the work.
Customer satisfaction matters too.
I feel satisfied in my new home.

examples.ko: 높은 점수가 주는 만족감은 오래가지 않아요.
examples.en: The satisfaction from a high score doesn't last long.
Her face lit up with satisfaction.

examples.ko: 그는 만족감으로 가득 찬 얼굴로 웃었어요.
examples.en: He smiled with a face full of satisfaction.

explain: 만족은 '만족해요'처럼 마음에 든다고 말할 때 쓰고, 만족감은 그때 드는 느낌 자체를 말해요. '만족감을 느끼다/주다/높이다'처럼 같이 쓰는 동사가 정해져 있어요. '뿌듯함'은 해냈다는 자랑스러움이 더 들어 있어요.
explain_en: 만족 is used to say you are pleased, as in 만족해요, while 만족감 names the feeling itself. It pairs with verbs like 만족감을 느끼다, 주다, and 높이다. 뿌듯함 carries more of a proud feeling of having achieved something.

examples.en: My nephew is three months old.

examples.ko: 생후 일 년쯤 되면 아기들이 걷기 시작해요.
examples.en: Around one year after birth, babies start to walk.

examples.ko: 강아지는 생후 두 달 뒤에 새 집으로 보낼 수 있어요.
examples.en: A puppy can be sent to a new home two months after birth.

examples.ko: 이 우유는 생후 6개월부터 먹일 수 있어요.
examples.en: You can feed this milk from six months after birth.

examples.ko: 생후 한 달 된 고양이를 병원에 데려갔어요.
examples.en: I took a one-month-old kitten to the vet.
The hospital does a test within 24 hours of birth.

explain: 아기나 새끼 동물의 나이를 '생후 3개월'처럼 개월 수로 말할 때 써요. 어른의 나이에는 쓰지 않고 '살'을 써요. 병원 안내문이나 육아 글에서 자주 보여요.
explain_en: It is used when giving the age of a baby or young animal in months, as in '생후 3개월'. It is not used for an adult's age, which is counted with '살'. You often see it in hospital notices and parenting articles.

en: nocturnal habit; nocturnality; being active at night

examples.en: Owls sleep during the day because they are nocturnal.
Cats are animals with a strong nocturnal nature.

examples.ko: 야행성 동물은 밤에 눈이 잘 보여요.
examples.en: Nocturnal animals can see well at night.
I am completely a night person.
I read a book that studied the nocturnal habits of bats.
My friend, who is a night owl, says morning classes are hard.

explain: 동물의 습성을 말할 때 쓰고, 반대는 '주행성'이에요. 사람에게는 '야행성 인간', '저녁형 인간'이라고 하고 반대는 '아침형 인간'이에요. 밤에 활동하는 동물이라서 '야행성 동물'이라고 자주 붙여 말해요.
explain_en: It is used for animal habits, and the opposite is 주행성. For people, 야행성 인간 or 저녁형 인간 is the night person, and the opposite is 아침형 인간. It often appears as 야행성 동물.

examples.en: They farm oysters in this area.
I met people who farm seaweed in the sea.
My father has farmed abalone since I was little.

examples.ko: 연어를 양식할 때는 물 온도가 중요해요.
examples.en: Water temperature matters when farming salmon.
Farmed fish is a little cheaper.

examples.ko: 좁은 곳에서 양식하다 보면 병이 쉽게 퍼져요.
examples.en: When you farm in a cramped place, disease spreads easily.

explain: 바다나 양어장에서 물고기·조개·김을 키워 거둘 때만 써요. 동물을 키울 때는 '키우다', 소나 돼지는 '사육하다'라고 해요. 바다에서 잡은 건 '자연산', 키운 건 '양식'이라고 구분해서 말해요.
explain_en: Only for raising fish, shellfish or seaweed in the sea or fish farms. For animals in general use '키우다'; for cattle or pigs, '사육하다'. At the fish market, wild-caught is '자연산' and farmed is '양식'.

examples.ko: 이 작가는 장편 소설을 많이 썼어요.
examples.en: This author has written many novels.
The first long work I wrote won an award.
I like long works more than short stories.
This comic was made as a long work.

examples.ko: 장편의 줄거리를 한 줄로 말해 보세요.
examples.en: Try describing the plot of the long work in one line.
I watched a feature-length animation on the weekend.

explain: 반대말은 '단편'이고, 중간 길이는 '중편'이에요. 소설·영화·만화·애니메이션처럼 이야기가 있는 작품에 쓰고, 노래나 짧은 글 하나에는 쓰지 않아요. '장편 소설'처럼 다른 말 앞에 붙여 쓰는 경우가 많아요.
explain_en: The opposite is '단편', and the middle length is '중편'. It is used for works with a story, like novels, films, comics, and animation, not for a song or a short text. It is often placed before another noun, as in '장편 소설'.

examples.en: This drama is very popular with middle-aged people.

examples.ko: 중년층을 위한 건강 프로그램이 새로 생겼어요.
examples.en: A new health program for the middle aged has started.
These days, middle-aged people use smartphones well too.
Most customers of this shop are middle-aged.

examples.ko: 중년층 취업 문제가 뉴스에 자주 나와요.
examples.en: The job problems of the middle aged often appear in the news.
The hobbies of middle-aged people have become more varied.

explain: '-층'은 비슷한 나이나 처지의 사람들 무리에 붙어서 '청년층', '노년층'과 함께 써요. 한 사람을 말할 때는 '중년'이라고 해요. 뉴스나 조사 결과에서 자주 보여요.
explain_en: The suffix '-층' attaches to a group of people of similar age or situation, as in '청년층' and '노년층'. For one person you say '중년'. You often see it in news and survey results.

examples.ko: 이 떡은 쫄깃쫄깃해서 계속 먹게 돼요.
examples.en: This rice cake is so chewy that I keep eating it.
The chewy noodles go well with the broth.
When I chew the squid slowly, a sweet taste comes out.

examples.ko: 삶은 지 얼마 안 돼서 아직 쫄깃쫄깃해요.
examples.en: It was boiled not long ago, so it is still chewy.

examples.ko: 쫄깃쫄깃하게 구운 닭 껍질이 제일 맛있어요.
examples.en: The chewy grilled chicken skin is the tastiest.
The ramen got soggy, so it isn't chewy.

explain: 부사지만 실제로는 '쫄깃쫄깃하다'나 '쫄깃쫄깃한 면'처럼 더 많이 써요. 면, 오징어, 떡, 고기처럼 탄력 있게 씹히는 음식에 쓰고, 찰기가 강하면 '쫀득쫀득'이라고도 해요. 칭찬하는 말이라 음식 후기에 자주 나와요.
explain_en: Although it is an adverb, people more often use it as '쫄깃쫄깃하다' or '쫄깃쫄깃한 면'. It describes foods that have a springy chew, like noodles, squid, rice cakes and meat; if it is more sticky and dense, people also say '쫀득쫀득'. It is a compliment, so it appears often in food reviews.

examples.en: Listening to the radio is my habit on the way to work.
The English listening test was hard.
If you send in a listener's story, they give you a gift.
I listen to the news every day as listening practice.
This program's audience ratings have risen a lot.
The recording was so fast that it was hard to follow.

explain: 일상에서는 '듣기'가 더 자연스러워요. '청취'는 방송이나 시험, 행사처럼 격식 있는 곳에서 써요. '청취자', '청취율'처럼 합쳐서 자주 말해요.
explain_en: In daily speech '듣기' sounds more natural. '청취' belongs to broadcasts, tests, and events. It often combines into other words such as '청취자' and '청취율'.

examples.ko: 결과를 보면 이 방법이 더 좋다고 판단돼요.
examples.en: Judging by the results, this method seems better.
It was judged unsafe, so we cancelled.
If it is judged dangerous, tell me right away.
Only people judged to have no problem go in.
It has not been judged exactly yet.
Please explain why it was judged that way.

explain: '-라고 판단되다' 모양으로 많이 나오고, 자료를 보고 결론을 낸다는 글말 느낌이에요. 일상 대화에서는 '그런 것 같아요'를 더 자주 말해요. 내가 판단하면 '판단하다'예요.
explain_en: It most often appears as '-라고 판단되다', and it has a written feel of reaching a conclusion from the evidence. In everyday talk, '그런 것 같아요' is more common. When you judge it yourself, use '판단하다'.

examples.en: Milk is a food with a high calcium content.
The ingredient label shows the amount of sugar.
I want to buy a product that contains vitamins.
Check the ingredients carefully.
We need to test whether it contains lead.

examples.ko: 이 제품은 색소 함유량이 0%라서 아이도 쓸 수 있어요.
examples.en: This product has 0% colouring content, so children can use it too.

explain: 함유는 어떤 성분이 안에 들어 있는 것을 말하는데, 주로 식품이나 화장품 포장, 설명서 같은 글에 나와요. '함유량', '함유 성분'처럼 뒤에 말이 붙는 경우가 많아요. 말할 때는 '들어 있다'가 훨씬 자연스러워요.
explain_en: Hamyu means a substance is contained inside, and it appears mainly in writing such as food or cosmetics packaging and manuals. It often takes a following word, as in 함유량 or 함유 성분. In speech, 들어 있다 sounds far more natural.

en: be a box-office hit; draw a big audience; show (commercially)

examples.en: That movie was a big hit as soon as it opened.

examples.ko: 이 드라마가 흥행하면 시즌 2가 나올 거예요.
examples.en: If this drama is a hit, season 2 will come out.

examples.ko: 공연이 흥행해서 추가 공연을 열기로 했어요.
examples.en: The show was a success, so they decided to add performances.
It's a work that didn't do well at the box office, but I like it.
Movies that do well in summer are usually action films.

examples.ko: 흥행할 줄 알았는데 관객이 별로 없었어요.
examples.en: I thought it would be a hit, but there weren't many viewers.

explain: 영화, 공연, 드라마가 관객을 많이 모으고 돈을 잘 벌 때 써요. 결과를 말할 때가 많아서 '흥행에 성공하다', '흥행에 실패하다'도 같이 알아 두세요. 책이 많이 팔리면 '베스트셀러가 되다', 노래가 인기를 얻으면 '히트하다'를 더 자주 써요.
explain_en: Used when a film, show or drama draws large crowds and makes money. It often describes results, so also learn 흥행에 성공하다 and 흥행에 실패하다 (succeed or fail at the box office). A book that sells well becomes a 베스트셀러, and a popular song is 히트하다.
